question: The Bhakti saint who propagated devotion to Rama in the Awadhi dialect was:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tulsidas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tulsidas** was a prominent Bhakti saint and poet, known for his devotion to Lord Rama and his literary contributions in the Awadhi dialect.
 
• He is best known for authoring the **Ramcharitmanas**, a retelling of the Valmiki Ramayana in Awadhi, making it accessible to the common people of India.
 
• Tulsidas's works emphasize devotion (Bhakti) and morality, playing a significant role in popularizing the worship of Lord Rama in northern India.
 
• He was a contemporary of Emperor Akbar and lived in the 16th century, actively promoting the Bhakti movement during his time.
 
• His other notable works include **Vinaya Patrika**, **Hanuman Chalisa**, and several other devotional hymns dedicated to Lord Rama and Hanuman.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kabir**
 
 
• Kabir was a 15th-century mystic poet and saint associated with the Bhakti and Sufi movements.
 
• His compositions, known as **Dohe** (couplets), emphasize the unity of God and criticize social evils such as caste discrimination and religious hypocrisy.
 
• He did not promote devotion to any specific deity and instead focused on Nirguna Bhakti (worship of a formless God).
 
• His works are compiled in the **Bijak** and also feature in the Guru Granth Sahib.
 
 
 
• **Surdas**
 
 
• Surdas was a 16th-century Bhakti poet and saint, renowned for his devotion to Lord Krishna.
 
• He is best known for his contributions to Krishna Bhakti literature, particularly his verses in the **Sursagar**.
 
• His works focus on the childhood and playful exploits of Lord Krishna, written in Braj Bhasha.
 
• Surdas is regarded as a key figure in the Krishna Bhakti tradition.
 
 
 
• **Namdev**
 
 
• Namdev was a 13th-14th century Bhakti saint from Maharashtra, associated with the Varkari tradition.
 
• He was a devotee of Lord Vitthal (a form of Lord Krishna) and composed numerous devotional hymns in Marathi and Hindi.
 
• Namdev’s verses are included in the Guru Granth Sahib, the holy scripture of Sikhism.
 
• His teachings emphasize devotion, equality, and the futility of ritualistic practices.
